subject.title: github-copilot: legacy OAuth token refresh sends bearer credential to unvalidated enterpriseUrl domain

question: Should unsafe legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth `enterpriseUrl` values fail closed at refresh, be normalized to `github.com`, or be repaired before runtime uses them?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the handling of already-persisted credentials is both a security-boundary and upgrade-compatibility choice that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Fail closed with doctor repair
options.body: Reject non-allowlisted legacy domains before any refresh request and add `openclaw doctor --fix` handling to explain and repair or clear unsafe stored values.

options.title: Runtime normalize only
options.body: Normalize unsafe legacy domains to `github.com` during refresh, reducing credential egress risk while leaving persisted state cleanup for a later pass.

options.title: Route through private security process
options.body: Pause public implementation detail until maintainers decide the disclosure, migration, and release handling for legacy credentials.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with doctor repair
recommendation.body: Reject non-allowlisted legacy domains before any refresh request and add `openclaw doctor --fix` handling to explain and repair or clear unsafe stored values.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans auth-profile persistence, doctor migration, and security policy, which match the strongest broad-history signal among the likely owners.
